narrative_problem: Nigeria's need profile is a productivity story before it is a technology story: a third of the workforce (1.3) produces cereal yields of 1,558 kg/ha (1.2), under two-fifths of the world average, while one person in five is undernourished (8.1). Two proposed context indicators sharpen the picture in opposite directions. Cereal import dependency is 16.3% (proposed indicator, not scored) because the staple basket is domestic — the wheat exposure that dominates the headlines is real but commodity-specific. Irrigation, meanwhile, equips 0.3% of agricultural land, leaving those yields hostage to rainfall.

The evidence base is deeper than the country's reputation for data scarcity suggests: post-harvest losses carry APHLIS cereal estimates of 9.5–17.4% (1.5), women's land rights the SDG 5.a.1 statistic of 31.6% (8.5), mobile money the 2025 Findex wave at 32.8% (8.4), foundational ID coverage 79.1% of adults (4.7), and rural connectivity a genuine rural figure of 48% 4G coverage (2.1). What remains unmeasured is farmer-facing: the gender balance of the digital-agriculture workforce (5.12), language coverage of digital services (8.11) and climate-advisory reach (8.17) are recorded gaps, and seven further indicators carry evidence but no level because what was found measures a different construct from what the indicator names. Nigeria measures its systems better than it measures their users. The binding constraint, though, is not evidence but the last mile: rural electricity reaches 23.5% of rural residents (2.9), and that single universal prerequisite caps every use-case column at Partial, however strong the rails above it.
narrative_register: The landscape is crowded and discontinuous: the two largest farmer-facing programmes (GES, ABP) are closed, NAGS-AP has taken over input support with the same registration-in-a-silo pattern, the national digital agriculture strategy has waited unadopted since 2020, and NIDAP — the vehicle meant to harmonise them — is early in rollout.

3.11: India's AgriStack published national agricultural data standards and registry schemas on digital ID rails — the standards mandate preceded the analytics ambition.
3.3: Rwanda's Smart Nkunganire consolidated input-subsidy registration onto one national platform.
2.9: Pay-as-you-go solar bundled with agricultural services is documented at scale across East and West Africa.
5.7: Kenya's Ministry of Agriculture stood up a dedicated digital unit ahead of its e-voucher scale-up — the delivery capacity preceded the program.
